claim.pdf_says: locae-name-1   [the printed standard, verified on the 300 dpi render of the locale-phrase-1 brace group, spells it with the 'l' missing - an ISO typographical defect; the locale-phrase-2 stack below it spells 'locale-name-2' correctly, as does syntax rule 3) on the same page]
claim.markdown_says: - `locale-name-1`   [silently corrected, with no note that the print is defective]
claim.why_it_matters: The corrected spelling is the right text to implement against (12.3.6.3 rule 3) 'Locale-name-1 and locale-name-2 shall be locale names defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph' confirms the intent), but the transcription is supposed to record ISO's own defects rather than quietly normalize them - otherwise a later reader who renders the page sees a mismatch and cannot tell whether the markdown or the print is wrong.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on two independent readings of the PDF, and the claim quotes both sources accurately.

(1) 300 dpi raster (E:/Temp/specrecon/v315/spec_p315.png), first brace group under 'where locale-phrase-1 is:', cropped to native resolution and 3x upscaled: the glyphs read l-o-c-a-e-hyphen-n-a-m-e-hyphen-1. There is no 'l' between the 'a' and the 'e'. The 'locale-phrase-2' brace group below it, cropped identically, reads l-o-c-a-l-e-hyphen-n-a-m-e-hyphen-2 with the 'l' present. So this is not a font-substitution or glyph-dropping artifact of the render pipeline: the same font renders 'l' after 'a' correctly twice on the same page (in 'locale-name-2', and in 'IS locale-phrase-1' inside the general-format figure).

(2) PDF content stream (pymupdf get_text('words') on page index 314), which settles it independent of any rasterizer. The spec's text layer uses a constant-offset obfuscated encoding (+0x22 for lowercase letters), so token character COUNTS and codes are preserved:
  - y=408.6 (locale-phrase-1 group): len=12, width 62.01 pt, codes 8e 91 85 83 87 01e6 90 83 8f 87 01e6 0373 -> l o c a e - n a m e - 1
  - y=524.2 (locale-phrase-2 group): len=13, width 64.89 pt, codes 8e 91 85 83 8e 87 01e6 90 83 8f 87 01e6 0374 -> l o c a l e - n a m e - 2
The first token is one character shorter and is missing exactly the 8e ('l') that the second token carries in position 5. The 2.88 pt width difference matches the advance of a lowercase 'l'. The defect is in ISO's own content stream, not in the rendering.

(3) Syntax rule 3) on the same page reads 'Locale-name-1 and locale-name-2 shall be locale names defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph', so ISO's intent is unambiguous and the markdown's spelling is the semantically correct one. Severity 'cosmetic' is right: nothing to implement differently.

(4) The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13751-13757, reproduced verbatim in the page-315 work unit) renders the group as 'A brace group containing: - `locale-name-1` ...' with no annotation. 'locae' appears nowhere in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, so the normalization is silent.

(5) The claim's premise about transcription policy checks out: this transcription has an established practice of flagging ISO's own defects in figure notes rather than normalizing them - e.g. ISO_COBOL.md:4613 on the LISTING directive ('the missing underline appears to be a typesetting omission in the standard and is reproduced here as printed') and :16294 on the LINKAGE SECTION ('the diagram prints `77-level-description-entry` while the meta-language term table ... lists the term as `77-level-entry`; both spellings are as printed in the standard'). The p315 figure note documents underlining and both levels of choice indicators in detail but omits this misprint, so the gap is an inconsistency with the transcription's own convention, not a matter of taste.

I looked for grounds to refute and found none: the 'missing' letter is not reflowed onto an adjacent line, it is not page-break furniture or wrapping or hyphenation, and neither source is misquoted. The only refutation angle is 'the difference does not change meaning' - true, and precisely why this is filed cosmetic - but the two documents do differ byte-for-byte on this token, and the finding is about recording that difference, which is the transcription's stated job.
verdict.corrected_description:
Accurate as filed; one clarification about the remedy and one about scope.

Remedy: the fix is an ANNOTATION, not a text change. The markdown should keep `locale-name-1` as the implementable spelling (12.3.6.3 rule 3 confirms the intent) and add a note to the 12.3.6.2 figure notes recording that the printed locale-phrase-1 brace group reads 'locae-name-1' (missing 'l') while the locale-phrase-2 group reads 'locale-name-2' correctly - matching the house style already used at ISO_COBOL.md:4613 and :16294. Reproducing the typo in the body text instead would be a regression, since downstream tooling and readers take the markdown as the term of reference.

Scope: the claim describes the markdown as showing '- `locale-name-1`', which is exact, but it is worth noting that the whole locale-phrase-1/-2 region is already a prose paraphrase ('A brace group containing:') rather than a reproduction of the printed brace figure - unlike the general-format figure above it, which is transcribed with box-drawing delimiters and full figure notes. So the lost typo sits inside a region whose figure fidelity is downgraded generally; the annotation should probably be attached to whichever note covers those two brace groups. This does not weaken the finding - the token still differs between the two documents by one character with no note - it only locates it.
